svg.title: Release rules CONWIP kanban DBR
svg.text: 02 – Release (order-start) rules: CONWIP, kanban and drum-buffer-rope (DBR) – card / signal loops, with our line values
Boxes = process steps, triangles = WIP, accent loops = information (cards / signals). Push (MRP) has no loop: work starts because a plan says so.
(1) CONWIP – constant WIP for the whole line
card returns when a unit leaves the line → a new unit may start (w cards = WIP cap, e.g. w = 40)
(2) Kanban – one loop per supermarket (pull from the customer step)
(3) Drum–buffer–rope – release at the pace of the bottleneck (drum = FINAL-01)
rope: release = drum schedule − (23.6 min upstream flow + 60 min buffer) = 1.39 h ahead → ≈ 24 units
(4) Throughput vs WIP of our line (Hopp & Spearman benchmarks): rb = 17.2 units/h, T0 = 1 744 s = 0.484 h, W0 = rb × T0 = 8.3 units
practical worst case: TH = w ÷ (W0 + w − 1) × rb
more WIP → little more output, much longer lead time
